source.publisher: Belfast Telegraph (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: returned unopposed: named for the division in the Returning Officer's notice, which declares the persons opposite whose names no votes are entered duly elected where no polls were taken (Belfast Telegraph, 4 June 1955)

note: Triennial election of Down County Council, polled Thursday 2 June 1955 (Belfast Telegraph, 1 June 1955: 'POLLING DAY - To-morrow 2nd JUNE'). Saintfield was the only contested division: the retiring member, Lieut.-Col. Perceval Price (Unionist), polled 1,543 against 843 for Mr. James Lilley, also Unionist. The other nineteen divisions were filled unopposed. The Returning Officer's notice of result (Belfast Telegraph, 4 June 1955) lists all twenty divisions and the candidate returned for each; it prints no party labels. Returned unopposed.
